summary: Iteration 7: Validated the fix for the reported bug 'update GitHub par ho gaya par app 'no update' bata raha hai' (PRIVATE repo => GitHub /releases/latest returns 404 without a token). Wrote /app/9x_security/test_iter7_updater_private_repo.py (19 tests) and ran full regression: test_engine.py (16) + test_iter5_diagnostics.py (6) + test_iter6_ffmpeg_fallback.py (9) + iter7 (19) = 50/50 PASS in ~26s. Confirmed: (1) updater.check_latest returns ('', None, '') on 404 (private-without-token / no release) - no exception; (2) on token flow the Bearer header is sent to _api AND the API asset 'url' field is returned instead of browser_download_url (required so the S3 redirect works for private assets, because requests auto-drops the Authorization header cross-host); (3) 401/403 raise RuntimeError whose Hindi message mentions the code + 'token'/'PRIVATE'/'rate limit' guidance; (4) tag v1.0.9 is stripped to 1.0.9; (5) LIVE GitHub public API: microsoft/terminal returns a non-empty tag + release page, torvalds/linux returns '' (no releases) - neither hit rate limit; (6) download() streams with Accept: application/octet-stream + Bearer <token> when token given; (7) main.py Updates tab has QLineEdit self.gh_token (Password echo, objectName 'github-token-input'), NO repo input widget, _save persists c['gh_token'], _check_update passes token=token or None to both check_latest and download, and the 'No release' dialog explains PRIVATE + github.com/settings/tokens + Contents: Read-only + make-public option; py_compile passes on main.py; (8) config.DEFAULTS['gh_token']=''; (9) sed-bake compatibility: updater.py still has anchor lines starting exactly with 'APP_VERSION = "' and 'DEFAULT_REPO = "', and simulating the CI sed patches on a copy produces an importable module with the substituted APP_VERSION/DEFAULT_REPO values.
action_items: Real end-to-end confirmation for the USER's private repo can only be done by the user (paste their fine-grained token in Settings > Updates, Contents: Read-only). All mockable + public-live paths are green here.

OPTIONAL nit: updater.check_latest treats HTTP 200 with tag_name=null (rare draft/prerelease-only listing) as tag='' via .get(...) or ''.lstrip - behaviour is safe (falls through 'No release' dialog) but consider a specific message. Non-blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: updater._api decodes r.json() unconditionally when r.content is truthy; if GitHub ever returns non-JSON for a non-200 body (e.g. HTML rate-limit page) this raises before the status-code branch. Wrap in try/except and pass {} to keep the (401/403/404/other) branches deterministic.

updater.download() has no size cap or timeout on the stream loop; a malicious/broken CDN reply could hang indefinitely. requests already has a socket read timeout=120 but for large assets consider a per-chunk watchdog or Content-Length sanity check.

main.py._check_update swallows every Exception into a generic message; distinguish requests.ConnectionError (offline) vs RuntimeError (GitHub said 401/403) with more targeted Hindi copy for a smoother UX.
config.py does NOT migrate/scrub legacy 'github_repo' key from previously saved configs; harmless (it's ignored) but worth cleaning up on save to avoid confusion when users inspect config.json.

updater.apply_update()'s _apply_zip path deletes zip_path via a bat script AFTER running - if the app crashes between xcopy and start, the update.bat still runs; consider logging a marker file so failed updates are diagnosable next launch.
test_credentials: N/A - no real GitHub token needed; private-repo flow verified via mocks. Live public calls to microsoft/terminal and torvalds/linux were unauthenticated and did not hit rate limit during this run.

rca of the issue: Reported bug: 'update build ho gaya github me par software se update kiya toh koi update nahi hai bata raha hai'. RCA: The GitHub REST endpoint GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest returns HTTP 404 when the repository is PRIVATE and the caller is unauthenticated (this is GitHub's standard behaviour - it does not distinguish 'no such repo' from 'not visible'). The 'Save to GitHub' repos that Emergent creates for users are private by default, so the app - which was calling the API without any Authorization header - always saw 404 and correctly interpreted it as 'no release published yet', hence the misleading 'no update available' dialog. Mitigation (implemented in this iteration's code, verified here): (a) updater.check_latest now accepts an optional token and sends 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' via _api; (b) main.py Settings > Updates now exposes a password-masked 'GitHub Token' field (objectName github-token-input) saved to config.gh_token, and passes it to check_latest + download; (c) when the API returns 404, the 'No release' dialog explicitly tells the user in Hindi that PRIVATE repos need a fine-grained token (github.com/settings/tokens, Contents: Read-only) OR the repo can be made public; (d) for token-authenticated download, updater._pick_asset picks the API asset `url` (not browser_download_url) because private asset downloads require going through /repos/.../releases/assets/{id} with the Bearer header (requests then correctly drops Authorization on the cross-host S3 redirect, letting the actual binary GET succeed). All the above are covered by iter7 unit tests + a live public-repo sanity check.
